'''Daniel Kressner''' (born 7 April 1978) is a German [[Numerical analysis|numerical analyst]]. He has a Chair of Numerical Algorithms and High Performance Computing in the Institute of Mathematics at [[EPF Lausanne]].<ref name="todd_cv"/><ref name="googlescholar">{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.epfl.ch/daniel.kressner/?lang=en|title=Personal Homepage|website=people.epfl.ch|access-date=2021-11-02}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Kressner was born in [[Karl-Marx-Stadt]]. He studied Mathematics at [[TU Chemnitz]] from 1997 to 2001 and gained his PhD from [[TU Berlin]] in 2004. His PhD thesis ("Numerical Methods and Software for General and Structured Eigenvalue
Problems") was supervised by [[Volker Mehrmann]].<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=81652}}</ref> He was appointed assistant professor in Applied Mathematics at [[ETH Zurich]] in 2007. In 2011, he was appointed tenure-track assistant professor in Mathematics at EPF Lausanne, where he became associate professor in 2012 and full professor in 2017. Kressner held visiting positions as an [[Emmy Noether Program|Emmy Noether Fellow]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] at the [[University of Zagreb]] in 2005 and [[Umeå University]] in 2006. In 2018, he was the John von Neumann visiting professor at the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref name="todd_cv"/>

Kressner has been the Editor-in-Chief of [[ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software]] in 2017, and he is on the editorial boards of journals including the SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and its Applications, [[SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis]], and [[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]].

==Research==
Kressner is best known for his work on numerical methods, in particular for linear eigenvalue problems,<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-28502-4|title=Numerical Methods for General and Structured Eigenvalue Problems|last1=Kressner|first1=Daniel|series=Lecture Notes in Computational Science and Engineering |publisher=Springer, Heidelberg|year=2015|volume=46 |isbn=978-3-540-28502-1|location=Lecture Notes in Computational Science and Engineering|doi=10.1007/3-540-28502-4 }}</ref> nonlinear eigenvalue problems, and low-rank approximation techniques for matrix problems.<ref name="googlescholar" />

==Recognition==
He has been awarded a second [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]] from the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] in 2007. In 2011 he received the John Todd Award from the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]].<ref name="todd_cv"/>

He was elected as a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], in the 2022 Class of SIAM Fellows, "for contributions in numerical linear and multilinear algebra and scientific computing".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2022-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2022 Fellows|date=March 31, 2022|work=SIAM News|access-date=2022-03-31}}</ref>
